terms.grammar: conjunction: the indicative for a plain fact, the subjunctive for what is expected, intended or prevented
evidence: Sen. Ep. 87.1: naufragium antequam nāvem ascenderem fēcī
Varr. RR 1.1.1: ut sarcinās conligam, antequam proficīscar ē vītā

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative or subjunctive like antequam
evidence: Quint. 1.12.9: nam et dociliōra sunt ingenia, priusquam obdūruērunt
terms.comment: Often split, prius … quam; also “sooner than, rather than” (Lewis & Short s.v. prius).

phrases.english: I was shipwrecked before I had even got on board

phrases.latin: annus enim octōgēsimus admonet mē ut sarcinās conligam, antequam proficīscar ē vītā
phrases.english: for my eightieth year warns me to pack my bags before I set out from life

phrases.latin: nam et dociliōra sunt ingenia, priusquam obdūruērunt
phrases.english: for minds are more teachable before they have hardened

sources: Lewis & Short: antequam · Lewis & Short: prius
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-cato, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there.
The quotation of Varro, Rērum rūsticārum 1.1.1, is from the appendix of the Latinitas loci collection on Cato (loci-cato).
